clue.text: Mistake made by Hereford plant?

indicators.note: made by places the mistake beside the Hereford, the animal word coming first

parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, so here a cow
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A cattle breeder's error at the Hereford farm turns out to be a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' puts the Hereford beside the mistake; the question mark flags a plant whose name looks like a cow's lip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula, a common British meadow plant.

clue.text: Legal adviser kept by the uncommunicative

definitions.meaning: a barrister or advocate representing a client
a secretive person keeps their own advice to themselves, in the idiom about keeping one's own

explanation.surface: A lawyer is retained by clients who say little.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is called counsel, and the idiom 'keep one's own counsel' means to stay silent about one's plans.

clue.text: Entertain with a couple of rhymes

definitions.text: Entertain with a couple of rhymes

parts.words: Entertain with a couple of rhymes
parts.note: a phrase for treating a guest lavishly that is made of two words which rhyme with each other

explanation.surface: A performer amuses the audience with some short verses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to entertain someone generously with food and drink, and its two key words rhyme.

clue.text: Initially little girl welcomes current break

indicators.note: welcomes means the girl's letters take in another piece among them
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word little

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A little girl lets an electric current in, causing a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes only L from 'little'; 'welcomes' has the girl's letters, with that L, take the current inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a gap or missing portion, a break in a text or sequence.

clue.text: Courage bringing power and good fortune

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
luckiness is the state of having good fortune

explanation.surface: Bravery that brings both strength and luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluckiness is spirited bravery, a synonym for courage.

clue.text: Awkward, being lean and bony

definitions.meaning: stiff and ungainly in movement or manner
thin, with sharp corners showing through

explanation.surface: Someone ungainly because they are thin and bony.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes both a gawky, stiff manner and a thin, sharp-featured body.

clue.text: Pain in first-class husband's inside

indicators.note: inside places the husband letter within the first-class word

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-rate
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A top-class husband is suffering a pain in his innards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Ring of light reveals East End tip, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the cockney phrase is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: a tip is a messy junk room, a glory hole, and an East End cockney drops the aitch

explanation.surface: Someone sees a halo shining over a London rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to cockney speech, which drops a word's opening H; 'it's said' turns the phrase into a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloriole is a halo or aureole, a ring of light round a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Grassland producing endless 18 dn

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: the answer to 18 down is defined there as a leak, so this cross-reference stands for leak

explanation.surface: A meadow that is producing an unending seepage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or open grassland.

clue.text: Tycoon's first role, to develop part of plant

indicators.note: develop means the letters grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Tycoon's

explanation.surface: A tycoon's first job is to develop part of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small root, a part of a plant.

clue.text: Vessel with ancient city's name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A pot bearing the name of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, a vessel.

clue.text: Telly addict viewed primate clutching article on grass

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the primate piece after the grass

parts.note: couch is a coarse grass, couch grass

indicators.note: clutching means the primate's letters hold the article inside

parts.note: a potto is a small African primate
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A TV fan watched a monkey holding something on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' sets the article inside the primate; 'on' in an across clue puts it after the grass. 'viewed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is a lazy person who spends hours watching television.

clue.text: Venomous type's main interest, taking in any number

definitions.note: read as 'Venomous type is', with the 's as a link

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: taking in means the interest word encloses the number letter

parts.note: sake means interest or benefit, as in 'for your sake'
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A poisonous creature's chief interest is said to involve some number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts N inside SAKE to give SNAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea snake is a venomous marine reptile, a dangerous type of serpent.

clue.text: Practical intelligence Prince Henry displayed as well

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness or practical sense
Hal is the nickname of Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: Prince Henry showed shrewdness besides.
explanation.definitionFit: Withal is an archaic word meaning in addition, besides.

clue.text: Awkward youth under restraint on Eastern vessel

parts.note: hobbled means having the legs tied, restrained
a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A clumsy youth is held captive on an Oriental ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbledehoy is an old word for a clumsy, gawky adolescent boy.

clue.text: Crime, having no end of pests in this shop

indicators.note: having means the crime word holds the shortened pests inside it

parts.note: an offence is a crime

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the pests word is lost

parts.note: lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing involving endless vermin in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' docks the pests' final letter, and 'having' wraps the crime round what is left. The definition leans on the whole clue: such a shop sells drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol for drinking elsewhere.

clue.text: Duck moves to back of foul-smelling bathing-beach

indicators.note: moves to back of means the duck letter shifts to the end of the smelly word

parts.note: olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling
a duck is zero in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck waddles to the rear of a stinking beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming place or bathing beach.

clue.text: Appropriate piece for equestrian equipment

parts.note: to snaffle is to appropriate, to take for oneself
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A fitting part for riding gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle bit is a simple jointed mouthpiece used on a horse's bridle.

clue.text: Pots required for bed and breakfast?

parts.note: the word pots turned over reads stop

explanation.surface: Cooking pans are needed for a guesthouse stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is an instruction which, carried out, gives 'Pots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a brief overnight stay on a journey, as at a bed and breakfast.

clue.text: Tinker grabs old violin, varying this in playful manner

indicators.note: grabs means the tinker's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a kit is a small pocket violin of earlier times

indicators.note: varying means the letters of this are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tinker seizes an antique fiddle and plays it in a lively way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges 'this'; 'grabs' has the tinker hold the violin and that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittishly means in a lively, frisky or playful way.

clue.text: Leak identified by incomplete cross-reference in book

definitions.text: identified by incomplete cross-reference in book
definitions.meaning: a book's cross-reference reads '...' followed by a number, so without the number it is incomplete

explanation.surface: A leak is pinned down by a half-finished note in a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly leaking out, and split it reads as a book's cross-reference.

clue.text: Reprimand directly

definitions.meaning: a ... is a rebuke, as in a ... on the wrist
... means straight or exactly, as in ... in the middle

explanation.surface: Tell someone off straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap means a rebuke as a noun and squarely or directly as an adverb.

clue.text: Current article in jotter is partly mine

indicators.note: in places the current and article letters inside the jotter word

parts.note: a pad is a notebook or jotter
I is the symbol for electric current
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A topical item in my notebook is partly my own.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithead is the top of a mine shaft and its surrounding buildings, part of a mine.

clue.text: Garment bachelor's put on smells awful

indicators.note: put on in a down clue puts the bachelor letter above the smelly word

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
reeks means stinks

explanation.surface: A bachelor's clothing gives off a terrible smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeks is a Scots word for breeches or trousers, a garment.

clue.text: Free former politician in case of embezzlement

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in puts the politician inside those outer letters
case of takes the outer letters of embezzlement, its first and last

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former MP is freed in an embezzlement case.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means free from an obligation or liability.

clue.text: It built up at first without university's guarantee

indicators.note: at first puts the built-up word ahead of It
without means the university letter is left out

parts.note: accrued means accumulated, built up
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something built up at first without a university's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the university letter from the built-up word, and 'at first' sets what remains before It.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to vouch for or officially guarantee someone's standing.

clue.text: Australian redhead down in the dumps

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang, a red-haired person is ironically called by a colour name

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired Australian is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is Australian slang nickname for a redhead, and also means sad or depressed.

clue.text: Mixed feelings girl revealed in certain surroundings

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the surroundings word

parts.note: an ambience is the character of particular surroundings
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl shows conflicted emotions in a particular setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambivalence is the state of having mixed or contradictory feelings.

clue.text: Plot a society girl overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society woman

explanation.surface: A debutante's scheme is foiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed is a garden plot for flowers or vegetables.

clue.text: Report of excessive 'speed, once

indicators.note: report of means a spoken version, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: high means excessive, as in high prices

explanation.surface: News of excessive speed in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an archaic verb meaning to hasten, to speed.

clue.text: Approve quarters adjoining witch's place

indicators.note: adjoining means the quarters sit right beside the witch's place

parts.note: the Witch of Endor appears in the Bible's First Book of Samuel
S and E are two compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: Approving accommodation next to a witch's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or give support to something.

clue.text: Tried English journalist that's pinched spades, for example

indicators.note: pinched means these pieces have taken the others inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
S is spades in card games
say means for example

explanation.surface: An English journalist tried who'd stolen some spades, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' sets the spade letter and the 'for example' word inside E + ED, just after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Essayed means attempted, tried.
